caption: The drawing depicts a double wooden door set within a rectangular doorway with a slightly arched top. The doors are constructed from vertical wooden planks and feature decorative cutouts forming a repetitive geometric pattern of quatrefoil-shaped panels. The wood appears worn and weathered, with visible grain lines and some areas of discoloration in tones of brown and gray. The doorway surround consists of a combination of exposed red and brown bricks, as well as grayish mortar or plaster, indicating an unfinished or aged structure. The door sits above a floor made from terracotta-colored square tiles, with the front edge of the tiles visible. The background is a plain, off-white or light beige color without additional detail. There is a small signature and date in the lower right corner near the base of the doorway.
title: Church Doors
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
